SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2025-040, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE TO ACCEPT THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY AFFORDABLE HOUSING SOLUTIONS
  AGENCY (LACAHSA) MEASURE A FUNDS

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2025-040, a resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale to accept the LACAHSA Measure A Funds; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or their designee to execute any documents related
  to the application, acceptance, and implementation of approved grant programs
  and projects of the LACAHSA Measure A Funds.

BACKGROUND

On November 5, 2024, voters supported Measure A, a half-cent sales tax that will sunset
Measure H, a quarter-cent sales tax passed by the voters in 2017 to address
Homelessness. Generating over $1 billion annually, Measure A funding will be shared
between Los Angeles County (County), cities, and Councils of Government, the Los
Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), and LACAHSA.

LACAHSA was created to make housing more affordable, help people stay in their
homes, and increase housing options for people experiencing homelessness. It is a
regional organization focused on County and comprised of leaders, including the County
Supervisors, elected officials representing cities countywide, and nonprofit and
community leaders.

Re: Resolution No. CC 2025-040
May 21, 2025

DISCUSSION

LACAHSA has allocated $1,964,308 to the City of Palmdale for affordable housing
creation, preservation, prevention, and ownership. Activities will be identified based on
guidelines to be provided by LACAHSA, including ensuring that 70% is expended within
a 2-year period.

FISCAL IMPACT

$1,964,308; The LACAHSA Measure A Funds allocation is $1,964,308 for Fiscal Year
2025-26. Funding will be allocated to the City in subsequent years.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  C. Pursue alternative financing opportunities for continued infrastructure
  improvements and quality community programs.

SUBJECT:  AWARD AND APPROVE AGREEMENT WITH HATHAWAY-

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Award and approve Agreement No. A-8949 with Hathaway-Sycamores Child and
  Family Services (Sycamores), for transitional mental health services in an
  amount not to exceed $2,175,000 for a term of 24 months for the period of July
  1, 2025 through June 30, 2027; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute Agreement No. A-8949 with
  Sycamores, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The City Council has approved a dedicated allocation of funding aimed at addressing a
significant gap in the continuum of mental health services—specifically for residents who
require transitional support after experiencing a mental health crisis. This funding will
support the development and expansion of programs designed to assist individuals who,
while not meeting the legal threshold for involuntary psychiatric hospitalization (such as
a 5150 hold), are nonetheless in urgent need of stabilization, immediate care, and
ongoing therapeutic support. The initiative seeks to fill the void between emergency
intervention and long-term mental health care, providing essential services that help
prevent relapse, reduce repeated crises, and ease the burden on emergency rooms,
law enforcement, and families navigating complex mental health challenges.

May 21, 2025

DISCUSSION

An RFP was issued in September 2024, and the City received five proposals, which
were reviewed by an evaluation committee. The five bidders are listed below:

  Bidder  Location
  1. Community Development Center USA.  Palmdale, CA
  2. Hathaway-Sycamores Child and  Palmdale, CA
  Family Services
  3. Naderra Inc  Los Angeles, CA
  4. SALVA  Palmdale, CA
  5. Tele-Help, Inc.  San Diego, CA

Sycamores’ scope of work includes, but is not limited to:

    Provide a 24/7 crisis support system for intensive programs;
    Will have Mobile Crisis Outreach Teams (MCOT) staff in office and for field
  response Tuesday–Friday from 6 pm to 8 am and all day Saturday and Sunday;
    Ensure that there is in-person clinical support 8 hours a week, and include some
  evening hours for walk-in mental health crisis support;
    Sycamores will propose child and adult assessment/outcome tools for this
  program, which the City will approve;
    Schedule monthly sync-up meetings, including the City, Sycamores, Fire, and
  Sheriff Departments, at a minimum, with the option of bringing in additional referral
  entities as needed, such as hospitals. These meetings will be used to review data,
  identify successes, and implement opportunities for process improvement;
    Collaborate with the City to identify the data gathered for the program, such as
  demographics, level of equity, services provided, linkages, length of service, and
  service outcomes;
    Medication management will be provided through linkage to community resources.
  Sycamores will not directly provide medication management;
    Sycamores will actively work with the participants and their family members/
  support systems to empower them to navigate the system and learn how to access
  services in the future. Linkage may include finding an available provider,
  scheduling the appointment, or accompanying the participant to the appointment
  if needed; and,
    Sycamores will set the schedule of services with the City based on peak need
  utilizing data and provide 24/7 after-hours crisis support telephonically or virtually.

Sycamores’ demonstrated the highest level of quality and responsiveness to the
requirements outlined in the RFP. They clearly addressed all required duties,

responsibilities, and specifications and provided detailed and relevant information in each

    Provided evidence of experience delivering transitional mental health support

Sycamores has demonstrated extensive experience supporting individuals with intensive

short-term case management, peer support, and warm handoffs to long-term care—

This CONTRACT for services (“Contract” herein) is made and entered into by and
between the City of Palmdale, a public body corporate and politic, (hereinafter called
“CITY”), and HATHAWAY-SYCAMORES CHILD AND FAMILY SERVICES, a
PROVIDER, (hereinafter called “CONTRACTOR”). This Contract shall become

  RECITALS

  WHEREAS, CONTRACTOR represents that CONTRACTOR has the expertise
and is qualified to perform the services described in this Contract.

NOW THEREFORE, CITY and CONTRACTOR, in consideration of the mutual
covenants hereinafter set forth, agree as follows:

1  CITY PROJECT MANAGER

To provide the services required by this Contract, CONTRACTOR shall act under the
authority and approval of CITY MANAGER /designee, who shall oversee this
Contract, the work performed by CONTRACTOR, assist CONTRACTOR with any
necessary information, audit billings, and approve payments. The CONTRACTOR
shall channel all contacts and requests through the City project manager.

2  DESCRIPTION OF WORK

2.1  CONTRACTOR shall provide the following services in a manner satisfactory
to CITY:

• Provider will offer high-quality intensive therapeutical transitional mental health
services to individuals with a wide range of bio-psychosocial problems with a
recovery-focused treatment plan accompanied by appropriate psychiatric, medical,
case management, housing resources, and support.

• Increase access to care, decrease mental health symptoms, ease the stigma of
mental health, and reduce the toll mental illness takes on, families, the public,
organizations, and the social network of the community.

Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) and Service Monitoring

• Provide Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) Plan which outlines the process for
tracking, evaluating, and reporting outcomes at the individual and service levels.
Ensure that it is a results based performance tracking system.

 • Schedule monthly sync up meetings including the City, Sycamores, Fire Department
and Sherrif department at minimum with the option of bringing in additional referral
entities as needed such as hospitals. These meetings will be used to review data,
identify successes and opportunities for process improvement to be implemented.

• The City and Sycamores will work together in identifying what data is gathered for
the use of the program such as demographics, level of equity, services provided,
linkages, length of service and outcomes of the services.

• Administer outreach activities to encourage individuals and families to utilize the
services in the identified areas. These strategies should include outreach activities
and methods to engage people in treatment. Outreach should include contacts with
community groups such as Faith-Based organizations, neighborhood associations,
any law enforcement agency, the Los Angeles Sheriff Department MET, Los Angeles
County Department of Mental, Palmdale Regional Medical Center, and Antelope
Valley Medical Center.

• Provide a plan for working with persons from diverse cultures should include
information on mental health service strategies and resources to respond to the
specific needs and preferences of persons who live in the identified zip codes.

• Implement transitional mental health support services, including the following
elements:

a. Program Days and Hours: Services to be provided by telehealth or in-person.
Services will be no less frequent than at least 1x per month per individual, or services
may be provided more often than clinically indicated. The program sites are expected
to have crisis intervention capacity, including at least 24/7 off-hours telephonic
availability of a clinician who can perform remote crisis intervention, information
sharing, and coordination of care. All transitional client information is to be obtained
from previous providers.

Sycamores will set the schedule of services with the City based on peak need
utilizing data and provide 24/7 after-hours crisis support telephonically or virtually.

A triage assessment system to categorize the urgency of behavioral health needs is
required, using priority levels routine, urgent, and emergent.

The mental health outpatient clinic is expected to have at least eight hours per week
of open access time when individuals can walk in for an initial assessment.

The outpatient transitional mental health support clinic must provide information on
proposed screening and assessment processes, including specific screening tools
and instruments they plan to use with children and/or adults (it is also expected that

 all participants in the mental health outpatient clinic will be screened regularly for
substance use challenges, which include tobacco).

The City will also require that providers use specific structured screening and
outcome tools for adults if required and a separate tool for children and that the
impact of these structured tools be provided to the City continuously at an interval
and frequency to be determined by the City.

b. Recovery and Resilience-Focused Planning: The planning process for each person
receiving services should be strengths-based and collaborative. It should involve the
person participating in services, family/significant others, and other interdisciplinary
team members. Recovery and resilience-focused plans should be consistent with the
assessment results and include behavioral plans with measurable goals and
objectives.

c. Treatment: Individuals receiving services should be provided opportunities to
change mental health professionals with no penalty or loss of service within reason.
Appropriate medication use when indicated, as well as responsible medication
management and monitoring, are also essential. Medication management will not be
provided directly through Sycamores but will instead be facilitated through linkages to
community resources.

Providers are expected to describe how measures will be utilized to evaluate patient
treatment progress and outcomes. This includes how progress and outcomes will be
used to guide the discussion regarding any necessary modifications needed to
advance the service delivery of patient services.

d. Community Coordination and Integration: Services are expected to connect people
with their communities and assist them in utilizing existing community resources to
support and sustain recovery and ongoing resilience. The transitional mental health
support clinic is expected to assist members in learning about community resources.
As such they are expected to have resource information for relevant community
organizations.

Sycamores will actively work with the participant and their family members/ support
system to empower them to navigate the system and learn how to access services in
the future. Linkage may include finding available provider, scheduling the
appointment or accompanying the participant to the appointment if needed.

e. Continuing Support Planning: Planning for continuing support should begin at the
earliest possible moment after initial contact by a family member or other concerned
person, law enforcement personnel, or first responder, the patient him or herself prior
to program admission, be collaborative, and address areas such as but not limited to
the following: living situation, employment/education plans, medication list, follow-up

documentation that people were informed of the appropriate resources that promote
resilience and recovery and, whenever possible, were linked to those services and/or
supports.

f. Trauma: All staff must receive trauma-related training. Services must include
trauma screening for all individuals and trauma-related services as needed.

BACKGROUND

The City is required to adopt an operational budget each year that serves as the City’s
financial plan for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1 through June 30; and defines the City's
priorities for providing services to the community.

According to the Palmdale Municipal Code: Chapter 3.04 Budget Adoption Procedures,
the City Manager shall submit a proposed budget to the City Council no later than May
31 each year. Additionally, the City Council shall conduct a public hearing on the
proposed budget before adoption and shall adopt a budget prescribing the City’s
spending policy for the ensuing fiscal year annually on or before the thirtieth day of June.

DISCUSSION

In alignment with the City’s strategic plan, the draft Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2025-
26 is presented for your review and consideration.

The draft budget represents spending plans for all City funds, including General Fund,
Special Revenue Funds, Capital Project Funds, Internal Service Funds, and Enterprise
Funds.

GENERAL FUND

Revenues

  1. Property Taxes are anticipated to increase by 3% due to increases in the property
  tax base resulting from increased valuations and new development within the City.
  2. Sales Taxes are expected to increase by 58% due to the passage of Measure PD,
  which implemented a 0.75% increase in sales tax, effective April 1, 2025.
  3. Use of Property revenues are expected to increase by 6%, primarily due to leases
  of City-owned property and facility rental fees.
  4. Licenses and permits are expected to increase by 8%, primarily due development
  activity and timing of permit issuance.
  5. Development charges for services are expected to increase by 3% due to
  increases in plan checks and inspections anticipated in FY 2025-26.
  6. Other revenues are expected to increase in FY 2025-26 due to anticipated
  economic development property sales.

Expenditures

  1. Salaries and benefits are expected to increase by 6% year over year. This is the
  result of FY 2024-25 projections being reduced to account for vacancy savings
  that have been realized throughout the year. FY 2025-26 proposed budget would
  fully fund those positions that have been filled or are currently in recruitment
  phases. The FY 2025-26 salary and benefits include a proposed 4% increase (2%
  COLA and 2% wage increase) to employees.
  2. The LA County Sheriff Contract is expected to increase by 4.37%. However, the
  cost of the contract is being covered by multiple funding sources, including the
  General Fund and Measure AV. The liability portion of the contract is expected to
  increase from 12.5% to 13%, a 0.5% increase.
  3. The LA County Animal Care & Control contract is expected to increase by
  $800,000.
  4. Transfers to Reserves for FY 2025-26 include:
  a. $1 million contribution to the Pension Trust Fund to stabilize fluctuations in
  CalPERS rates; and
  b. $500,000 to fund the ongoing capital costs relating to maintenance and
  improvements of Drytown Water Park.

Terms
Accrual Basis – The method of accounting under which revenues and expenses are recorded when they occur,
regardless of the timing of related cash flows. Expenses are recorded at the time liabilities are incurred and
revenues are recorded when earned.
ACFR – The Annual Comprehensive Financial Report of the City which shows the financial status of the City.
Adoption – Formal action by the City Council that sets the spending limits for the fiscal year.
Appropriation – City Council authorization permitting the City to incur obligations and expend resources during
the fiscal year.

  Page 29 of 32
 Assessed Valuation – An official governmental value placed upon real estate or other property as a basis for
levying taxes.
Assessments – Levies that pay for improvements directly benefiting the property owners.
Audit – A review of the City’s accounts by an independent auditing firm to substantiate year-end fund balances,
reserves, and cash on hand.
Balanced Budget – The City’s operating revenues equal or exceed its operating expenditures.
Base Budget – Ongoing expense for personnel, contractual services, and the replacement of supplies and
equipment to maintain service levels previously authorized by the City Council.
Beginning / Ending Fund Balance – Unencumbered resources available in a fund from the prior/current year
after payment of the prior/current year’s expenses. This is not necessarily cash on hand.
Bond – A funding tool representing a written promise to pay a specific sum (face value or principal amount) in
the future (maturity date), plus interest. In local California government, bonds are only used to finance capital
improvements. There are two types of bonds:
General Obligation Bond – A bond requiring a 2/3 vote of the registered voters and backed by the full faith,
credit, and taxing power of the municipality.
Revenue Bond – A bond backed by either the revenue produced by the capital improvement or by commitment
of a specific revenue source.
Bond Proceeds – Debt issuances derived from the sale of bonds for the purpose of constructing major capital
facilities.
Budget – A financial plan listing proposed operational expenditures and revenue estimates for a particular time
period. The budget is proposed until it has been approved and adopted by the City Council. Palmdale’s budget
encompasses one fiscal year (July 1 to June 30).
Budget Message – A general discussion of the proposed budget as presented in writing by the City Manager to
the City Council. The message contains an explanation of principal budget items relative to the current year
adopted budget.
Capital Budget – The appropriation of bonds, operating revenue, or fees for improvements to City facilities
including buildings, streets, sewer lines, parks, traffic signals, drainage, etc.
Capital Improvement Program – A financial plan of proposed capital improvement projects with single and
multiple-year capital expenditures. The City of Palmdale's Capital Improvement Program is a ten-year plan,
which is updated annually.
Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) – A permanent addition to the City's assets, including the design, major
renovation, construction, or purchase of land, buildings, or facilities. This includes physical structural
improvements with a cost of $10,000 or more and a useful life of one year or more. Examples include a new
park, building modifications, traffic signals, resurfacing of streets and drainage improvements.
Capital Outlay – A budget category that budgets all equipment having a unit cost of more than $5,000. Capital
Outlay is budgeted in the operating budget as opposed to the capital improvement budget.
Contingency Fund – A budgetary reserve set aside for emergency or unanticipated expenditures.
Continuing Appropriation – Resources appropriated for a specific expenditure that is carried over from the prior
fiscal year.
Debt Ratio – Total debt divided by total assets. Used by Finance to assess fiscal health, internal controls, etc.
Debt Service – Payments of principal and interest on an obligation resulting from the issuance of bonds, notes,
or loans.
Debt Service Requirements – The amount of money required to pay principal and interest on outstanding debt
or to accumulate monies for future retirement of term bonds.

  Page 30 of 32
 Deficit – An excess of expenditures or expenses over resources.
Department – An organizational unit comprised of divisions or programs. This basic organizational unit of
government is functionally unique in its delivery of services.
Division – An organizational component of a department.
Encumbrances – Resources committed for future expenditures as a result of signing executory contracts such
as purchase orders and specific contracts for goods and services.
Enterprise Fund – An accounting entity that is financed and operated in a manner similar to private business
enterprises where the intent of the governing body is that the costs of providing goods and services to the
general public on a continuing basis is financed or recovered primarily through user charges.
Expenditure – The actual spending of funds set aside by an appropriation.
Fiscal Year – A 12-month accounting period used by the City. The City of Palmdale’s fiscal year begins July 1
and ends June 30.
Full Time Equivalent Position (FTE) – A part-time position converted to the decimal equivalent of a full-time
position based on 2,080 hours per year. For example, a part time typist working 20 hours per week would be
equivalent to 0.5 of a full-time position.
Fund – An independent fiscal and accounting entity with a self-balancing set of accounts to record revenue and
expenditures.
Fund Balance – The amount of financial resources available for use.
GAAP – Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. Uniform standards for financial accounting and recording,
encompassing the conventions, rules and procedures that define accepted accounting principles.
GASB – Governmental Accounting Standards Board is the current standards setting board for governmental
GAAP.
General Fund – The primary fund of the City used to account for all revenues and expenditures related to
municipal services and maintenance. Examples of departments financed by the General Fund include the City
Council, Finance, Planning and Law Enforcement.
General Obligation Bond – A bond requiring a 2/3 vote of the registered voters and backed by the full faith,
credit and taxing power of the municipality. This type of bond is used to finance capital improvements in local
California governments.
Goal – A statement of broad direction, purpose or intent based on the needs of the community. A goal is
general and timeless; that is, it is not concerned with a specific achievement in a given time period.
Grant – A contribution by a government or other organization to support a specific purpose, activity, or facility.
Infrastructure – Facilities upon which the continuance and growth of a community depend such as roads,
sewers, public buildings, parks, etc.
Interfund Transfers – The reallocation of money from one fund to another. The receiving fund must spend the
transferred money in a way that complies with any restrictions placed on the money when it was originally
received by the donor fund.
Investment Policy – A written, Council adopted policy delineating permitted investments of the City’s idle cash.
The City of Palmdale Investment Policy is typically updated and reaffirmed annually.
Major Fund – Any fund whose revenues or
expenditures, excluding other financing sources and uses, constitute more than 10%
of the revenues or expenditures of the appropriated budget.
Modified Accrual Basis – The accrual basis of accounting adapted to the governmental fund type spending
measurement focus. Under it, revenues are recognized when they become both measurable and available to
finance expenditures of the current period. Expenditures are recognized when the related fund liability is
incurred.

 Municipal Code – A book that contains City Council approved ordinances currently in effect. The Code defines
City policy with respect to areas such as planning, business licensing, etc.
Objective – Desired output-oriented accomplishments that can be measured and achieved within a given time
frame. Achievement of the objective advances the activity and organization toward a corresponding goal.
Operating Budget – Annual appropriation of funds for ongoing program costs including salaries and benefits,
services and supplies, debt service, capital outlay, and capital improvements.
Operating Expenditures – Expenditures for materials, supplies, and services which are ordinarily consumed
within a fiscal year and which are not included in departmental inventories.
Ordinance – A formal legislative enactment by the City Council that has the full force and effect of law within
City boundaries unless preempted by a higher form of law. An ordinance has a higher legal standing than a
resolution.
Palmdale Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) – The Palmdale CCA was formed in April 2019 through
California Choice Energy Authority (CalChoice) via City Council resolution to purchase power on behalf of the
City’s residents.
Palmdale Community Foundation – A 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization organized under the California Nonprofit
Public Benefit Corporation Law for public purposes.
PERS – Public Employees Retirement System.
Personnel – A budget category used to account for employee compensation including wages, salaries and
fringe benefits such as health, life, and disability insurance, retirement, and car allowance/mileage.
Program – A group of related activities performed by one or more organizational units for the purpose of
accomplishing a function.
Property Tax – An ad valorem tax on real property based upon the value of the property.
Property Transfer Tax – A tax imposed whenever the ownership of real property changes.
Reimbursement – Payment of amount remitted on behalf of another party, department, or fund.
Reserve – An account used to indicate that a portion of a fund's balance is legally restricted for a specific
purpose and is, therefore, not available for general appropriation.
Resolution – A special order of the City Council having a lower legal standing than an ordinance.
Resources – Total amounts available for appropriation including estimated revenues, fund transfers, and
beginning fund balances.
Revenue Bonds – A bond usually issued to construct facilities that is backed by either the revenue produced
by the capital improvement or by commitment of a specific revenue source.
Revenues – Money received by the City from taxes, fees, permits, licenses, interest, etc. or from other
governments during the fiscal year.
Special Revenue Funds – A fund used to account for revenues that are restricted in use by the City, State, or
Federal Government.
Subventions – Intergovernmental revenues paid to the City by another government, such as the State.
Transfer – A transfer is a transaction whereby the fund receiving the revenue transfers money to the fund
expending the revenue. An example would be an operating transfer from a Special Revenue Fund to the
Capital Projects Fund for construction expenditures.
User Fees/Charges – Charges of a voluntary nature paid by the person receiving the service in exchange for
the fee.
